solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Do well by one in California

parts.note: 'well' and 'so' both open a remark, as in 'So, what now?'

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other's letters

parts.note: a standard abbreviation of the US state
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone praises a person who has prospered out in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb opening an instruction, but it is the noun for a party, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal party or gathering, which is what a do means in British usage.

clue.text: Waste career for sports day fun?

parts.note: to sack a town is to lay waste to it
to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: Someone laments throwing away a career for a frivolous school event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb meaning to rush headlong. A sports day is a school athletics event in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race, hopping in a sack, is a classic novelty event at a school sports day.

clue.text: Sweet clown that's famous recently ringing husband

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown
H is the abbreviation for husband
late means recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured famous clown has lately phoned her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown (Nicolai Poliakoff) was a celebrated performer with Bertram Mills Circus in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate is an individual sweet, a confection, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Cross being in rising deep cuts

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upward, so the word runs backwards
being in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
a cross is shaped like X

explanation.surface: A crossing found within an upward run of deep cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep cuts' looks like a single phrase, but deep is the wordplay and cuts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut it drastically, so axes is cuts as a verb.

clue.text: Frightfully bad one if real

indicators.note: something frightfully done is in a terrible state, so the letters following are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a dreadfully bad person would be one if they were genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' reads as a conditional in the surface, but its letters belong to the jumble, leaving 'real' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for 'in good faith' and describes something genuine rather than fake.

clue.text: Liberally lubricate fuel pump

parts.note: to oil a part is to lubricate it
generously or liberally, as in 'well oiled'

explanation.surface: Advice to grease a petrol pump generously.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in reverse order: lubricate, then liberally.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a shaft pumping crude oil, the raw material of fuel, from the ground.

clue.text: Spruced up our ute and a van in natural style?

indicators.note: spruced up means tidied and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, leaving out 'and'

explanation.surface: Someone smartens up their utility truck and a van in an organic look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins the two vehicles in the fodder. A ute is a utility truck in Australian usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Nouveau was a decorative style built on flowing plant and other natural forms, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I do business — perfect

parts.note: taken as written
to deal is to trade or do business

explanation.surface: A trader boasts that their work is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly as wished, a synonym of perfect.

clue.text: Red diesel to some extent swirls

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so a portion of the words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Coloured farm fuel swirls about in its tank.
explanation.walkthrough: Red diesel is dyed, lower-taxed fuel for farm vehicles in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddies are currents of water or air moving in circles, so they are swirls.

clue.text: Close to this oar I drifted round loch?

definitions.text: Close to this oar I drifted round loch?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around another piece
something drifted has wandered from place, so the letters move about
close means the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its final letter
the letters to be rearranged
L is the abbreviation for loch on maps

explanation.surface: A rower near this oar drifted around a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too, with the question mark: whoever is close to the oar, drifting round a loch, is a sailor. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is someone who handles a boat on water, just the figure the scene describes.

clue.text: Wind up cold with each near miss

parts.note: to wind up a meeting is to close it
C for cold, as on a tap
as in a score of two all, two each

explanation.surface: A cold spell ends, and everyone has narrowly escaped something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' gives ALL through sports scores: 'two all' means two each.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is an idiom for a narrow escape from danger, exactly a near miss.

clue.text: Time to study stamp

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: It is time to look at a postage stamp under examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to put a foot down heavily, which is to stamp.

clue.text: Do stream without bishop

indicators.note: without means going lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a brook is a small stream
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: An instruction to treat a river without involving the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' here is the slang verb for cheat, as in 'I've been done'. Rook also nods to chess, alongside the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle or cheat them, a slang sense of do.

clue.text: Quaint European behind odd Orwell novel

indicators.note: behind says the first piece follows the rest at the end
novel means new, so the words just before it are made into something fresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone finds a European figure trailing behind a strange book by George Orwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' tempts as the noun book by Orwell, but it is an adjective signalling the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Olde worlde is a jokey mock-archaic spelling for things charmingly old-fashioned, that is, quaint.

clue.text: One maiden on the top of Greek building's bar

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so pieces are stacked in order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M abbreviates maiden, a cricket over with no runs
the triangular gable crowning a classical Greek temple front

explanation.surface: A young woman perches on the roof of a Greek temple.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle or hindrance, which is what a bar is as a noun.

clue.text: Siren, say, is constant — one's likely to hurt

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
one who harms

explanation.surface: A warning that a siren is ever-present and probably dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The mythical Sirens lured sailors to their deaths, so the surface's danger fits; 'say' marks a siren as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is an alluring, seductive woman, an example of a charmer who captivates people.

clue.text: Fun duty is full of it

indicators.note: a thing full of something holds it inside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a levy is a tax or duty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a fun job is full of something unsaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Levity is light-hearted humour or frivolity, so it means fun as a noun.

clue.text: Driver of commerce didn't wear being exploited

indicators.note: exploited means used and worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A commercial chauffeur refused to wear something because they felt used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist, but here it is a force that drove sailing ships of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds are steady tropical winds that historically propelled merchant sailing ships along trade routes.

clue.text: Cask greedily hangs onto froth

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it greedily
the head on a beer is its froth

explanation.surface: A barrel greedily keeps hold of the foam on its beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large barrel, a cask traditionally holding beer or wine.

clue.text: Admire son slipping away from retreat

indicators.note: slipping away means leaving, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: an army in retreat is in reverse
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent admires a son who quietly leaves a religious retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep respect, a stronger synonym of admire.

clue.text: Passage is in poem

indicators.note: in means inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: an epode is a lyric poem form
taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary passage appears inside a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: An epode is a classical lyric form, famously used by Horace, of alternating long and short lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a section or incident in a longer narrative, so a passage of it.

clue.text: Support Victor facing trouble for boasting?

indicators.note: facing means set directly in front of, so pieces stand side by side

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone backs a man named Victor who is in trouble for bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that bravado is closer to swagger than boasting proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness intended to impress, close to boastful swagger.

clue.text: Premium ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reward or bonus payment
second meaning: the naval vessel famous for its mutiny

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a top-quality vessel; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounty is a reward payment, and HMS Bounty is the ship whose crew mutinied under Captain Bligh.

clue.text: Sally under a female is nervous

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so it comes after the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
a sally is a sudden sortie or raid

explanation.surface: A woman named Sally, working beneath another woman, is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' poses as a woman's name, but it is a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid means fearful or anxious, close in sense to nervous.

clue.text: Especially picky if a studio's trashed

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fussy person would be extra demanding if their studio were wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastidious describes someone very concerned with detail and hard to please, which is especially picky.

clue.text: What kicks off showy theatrical being a mischievous monkey?

indicators.note: what kicks off is what starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its first letter
camp means exaggeratedly theatrical

explanation.surface: A flamboyant performer is acting like a naughty little primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey' is the affectionate term for a cheeky child, not a primate.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a playful, mischievous child, just what a cheeky little monkey means colloquially.

clue.text: For example, among first and last of ludicrous members

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece goes inside the other
first and last pick just the two end letters of the word that follows

parts.note: its end letters
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: An example drawn from among the first and last of some absurd club members.
explanation.definitionFit: Members is a formal word for limbs, so legs are members of the body.

clue.text: Fraudulently manipulate a capital

parts.note: to rig an election is to fix it fraudulently
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cooks the books to steal money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money in the surface, but it is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia.

clue.text: Love silver primate

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Someone adores a monkey made of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Agape here is the Greek word for selfless, Christian love, pronounced in three syllables, not the 'mouth open' word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape is the Greek term used in Christian theology for unconditional, selfless love.

clue.text: With respect to fine diamond being at risk

parts.note: on means about or concerning
fine thread is thin
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A precious diamond is described as being in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on thin ice is an idiom for being in a precarious or risky situation.

clue.text: Assistants in uniform filling department that is small

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a standard abbreviation of department
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
i.e. abbreviates the Latin for that is
S for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Helpers in uniform are packed into a department that happens to be tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputies are people appointed to act for or assist a superior, so they are assistants.

clue.text: Open loo was good enough

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet
as in 'that did', meaning it sufficed

explanation.surface: A toilet left open was considered adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: A loo is the British informal word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and honest, an open way of speaking.
